title: Write a ratio to compare two quantities (3:2, 3 to 2)

lesson.title: Ratios: Comparing Two Amounts

steps.say: You already know how to show a fraction of a set, like three out of five apples. Today we learn a different way to compare two groups: a ratio. A ratio tells us how many of one thing there are for every so many of another thing.

visual.caption: Two groups: one red apple, one green apple

steps.say: Imagine you have three red apples and two green apples in your lunch bag. To compare them, we say the ratio of red to green is three to two. We write it with two dots in the middle, like this: three colon two. The dots just mean the words to.

visual.caption: 3 red apples compared with 2 green apples

steps.say: Here is the most important part. The order of the numbers must match the order of the words. Red comes first in the sentence, so the number of red apples comes first in the ratio. Three red, two green, gives us three to two.

visual.caption: 3 red apples — the first number in red to green

steps.say: Let us try a real one. At a Vancouver bus stop there are four grown ups and six kids waiting. The ratio of grown ups to kids is four to six. And if someone asks for the ratio of kids to grown ups instead, we flip it around to six to four, because now kids are named first.

visual.caption: 4 grown ups and 6 kids at the bus stop

steps.say: Now the mistake I see all the time. A student sees three red counters and two blue counters, then writes two to three for red to blue. Oops! They wrote the blue number first. Always read your own sentence again: red to blue means red's number, then blue's number. Three to two is correct, and two to three would actually be blue to red.

visual.caption: Red is named first, so 3 goes first: 3:2

steps.say: So remember: a ratio compares two amounts, and the words tell you the order. Whoever is named first, their number goes first.

lesson.answer: A ratio compares two amounts — the one named first goes first, so 3 red and 2 blue is 3:2.

practice.question: At a Burnaby farmers market, a bag holds 5 groups of carrots with 1 carrot in each group, and 3 groups of potatoes with 1 potato in each group. Draw the groups if it helps! What is the ratio of carrots to potatoes? And what is the ratio of potatoes to carrots?
practice.answer: Carrots to potatoes is 5 to 3, written 5:3. Potatoes to carrots is 3 to 5, written 3:5 — the number flips because potatoes are named first.
